name: Finland (Helsinki)
kernel_gaps: a credit spread over several taxes in proportion after the state tax (työtulovähennys TVL 125 § 1 mom; alijäämähyvitys 132-133 §, at most 3/4 from the state tax first)
a credit phased in on one base (18 % of work income) and withdrawn on another (puhdas ansiotulo) at two successive rates (2,22 % then 3,44 %)
a capped deficit credit with child increases and transfer of the unused credit and maximum between spouses (TVL 131-134 §)
a levy with a cap (yleisradiovero: 2,5 % above 15 150 EUR, max 160 EUR) and a contribution on the difference of two bases (sairaanhoitomaksu 0,39 % extra)
an income-type split that depends on an asset value (unlisted dividends: 8 % of net assets, 25 % / 85 % capital, 75 % earned; TVL 33 b §)

validation.referee: OECD Taxing Wages 2025 (FIN, 8 family types x CGTC, CGITLETC, CGITFP, SLT, EECSSC, CTGG + take-home pay)
validation.notes: lines computed at the OECD's average municipal rate 7,54 % (oecd_map.py reads the exe's oecd754_* detail); 48/48 lines and 8/8 mapped take-home pays within 1 EUR; the contract net at Helsinki 5,30 % differs by 2,24 % of taxable income (M1) and equals the OECD THP within 0,02 EUR when run at 7,54 % (runs/referees.json oecd754_thp 8/8); the OECD books the YLE tax (160) in CGITFP

validation.referee: Veronmaksajat, Palkansaajan veroprosentit 2025 (wage earner, 7,54 % + church 1,38 %, 1 000-950 000 EUR)
validation.notes: annual taxes and contributions; max difference 0,50 EUR (their whole-euro rounding); harness/referees.py

validation.referee: Kela, Kokonaiseläkkeen ja nettoeläkkeen määrät 2025 (pension tax, single and couple, 7,54 %)
validation.notes: monthly tax to the cent (max difference 0,005 EUR/month); work + national + guarantee pensions

validation.referee: Verohallinto, automatically computed deductions 2025 (published thresholds and maxima)
validation.notes: eläketulovähennys max 11 030 and end 48 930; perusvähennys end 26 976; 65+ work credit 4 425: theorems in FiTax/Tests.lean

headline: Finland 2025 reproduces the OECD (48/48 lines), Veronmaksajat's 287-row table and Kela's 32-row pension table exactly; the 2025 work credit, still withdrawn up to 125 240 EUR of pay, pushes marginal rates above the top rate and makes bunching pay (950 EUR), an owner's dividend above the 8 % net-asset return is earned income that can be personally tax-free (so more net assets can cost more), and two government proposals state pay thresholds as net-income thresholds.
